about: Word lists the checker reads (WORDS-01 to WORDS-05, REASON-04, GEN-06, GEN-07, GEN-12, FORM-08, FORM-13) and the word list of blueprint 5.7 as data. Written by WP1 on 2026-09-28. Every list names its research source; entries marked [judgement] extend a research list in its own spirit.

flag_modes.always: WORDS-02 flags the word in field values and in user-facing text, outside double quotes that match the story.
flag_modes.user_text: Flagged only in user-facing text: everything above a file's divider, reports, the book, reference/07 and checkpoint messages.
flag_modes.in_fields: Flagged only in the fields named in in_fields ('*.origin' means the origin field of any record type).
flag_modes.field_name: A retired field or sub-part name: FORM-03 reports it with 'did you mean' the replacement, and the tidy fix renames it when the replacement is a single field (FORM-13).
flag_modes.prompts: Flagged only in compiled prompt text (GEN-12).
flag_modes.context: Not flagged by code: the word is too common or is used correctly elsewhere. Writers of cards, steps and messages still avoid it in the retired sense.
flag_modes.rule: Handled by another check or list, named in note.

exemptions.word: unit symbols after a number: s, min, %, $
exemptions.why: the blueprint's own user messages use them (13.3: '15 s', 'about 1 min 36 s', '$10')

mood_only_phrases.source: REASON-04's list (blueprint 7.2; craft-first CR04), B3 R23, B2 §12 and its failure table, B2 §4.8
mood_only_phrases.rule: REASON-04 (error): a why that contains one of these phrases fails; 'to emphasise' counts only with no object. The feeling words below fail when the why names nothing else: no quote from the scene, no ID and no named element (REASON-03 and REASON-04 together).
mood_only_phrases.mood_words_rule: These feeling words fail only when the why names nothing else: no quote from the scene, no ID and no named element (B3 R23; REASON-03 and REASON-04 together).

conditional.flag_when: no object follows ("to emphasise" at the end, or followed only by a mood word)

emotion_adjectives.source: A3 R2 and P3 (Weston: 'result direction is inaccurate direction'), C3 L07, D15 R1, C2 §2 drift note, A2 failure table
emotion_adjectives.rule: WORDS-01: an emotion adjective in does or task is an error; write two or three visible behaviours instead (C3 §6 method).
emotion_adjectives.judgement: the rest extend the research examples [judgement]

expression_words.source: B5 fixed description rules (no expression), C2 §2 (face mechanics, never an emotion word), K26 (C3's example keys superseded)
expression_words.rule: WORDS-05: a fixed description with an expression word is an error.

image_side_words.rule: Image-side words are never stored in state lines or fixed descriptions; code derives image sides per shot. Own sides (own left, her right hand) and 'hand nearest the camera' are allowed.

banned_prompt_words.source: B2 §4.8 and §12 failure table; D5 style bible banned words; B5 §6.2 rule 7 and mistake 17; C2 cliché pull; blueprint 8.5 (creature lint); K19
banned_prompt_words.rule: GEN-12: a banned word in a prompt is an error; describe the visible quality instead.
banned_prompt_words.exempt: words inside double quotes of the script, which never reach a prompt anyway

prompt_substitutions.source: K19 and B2 (torch), C3 R13 and L23 (falling), blueprint 8.1 phrasebook note (lens millimetres), B5 §6 identity key revision (humanoid)
prompt_substitutions.rule: Applied by the compiler (8.1 rule 5); PROJECT.prompt_words adds a project's own swaps.

swaps.to: visible evidence of the motion ("hair, cloth and straps drift up; nothing settles")
the phrasebook's lens words ("85 mm" becomes "compressed background, shallow focus")

unreliable_camera_terms.rule: Never trusted to words: split into two shots, composite, or use a guide video (8.5).

allowed_negations.rule: GEN-07: negation of a visible thing is an error outside these documented lines and a model's negative field.

named_reference_markers.rule: No real person, living artist, film title or brand in any field compiled into prompts; these phrases signal one.

shortening_markers.rule: FORM-08: a shortening marker inside a record is an error, unless inside double quotes that match the story.

abbreviations.rule: WORDS-04: an abbreviation or internal code in user-facing text is a warning. Write the full words.

field_name_synonyms.source: the retired field names of 5.7; FORM-03 suggests the replacement and FORM-13 applies it when it is a single field

value_synonyms.source: common shot-list abbreviations and spellings (B1 size ladder; 5.7 shot sizes); tidy fixes are logged as FORM-13
value_synonyms.rule: Applied only to the named field (and to sub-parts with the same key); every other spelling is FORM-04 with 'did you mean'.
